key_insight: A multispectral metasurface combined with a hybrid CNN-ViT model can detect skin cancer more accurately by capturing both spectral and spatial lesion features.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support faster, portable, and more sensitive skin lesion screening than conventional RGB-based imaging, especially for early-stage disease.
method: Noninvasive multispectral imaging using a designed metasurface
Hybrid deep learning with CNNs for local features and Vision Transformers for global context
Attention maps used to highlight clinically relevant lesion regions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based performance of about 98% accuracy, 95% sensitivity, and 99% specificity, outperforming RGB-only and single-architecture methods.
watch_item: The results are simulation-based, so real-world clinical validation and hardware integration remain important before deployment.
paper_title: Intelligent Skin Cancer Detection Using a Multispectral Metasurface and a Hybrid
